title: Gated Cascade Experimentation Lab (working notes)
body:
Purpose: quick brain-dump & operational sketch for running multi-stage, cross-service canaries ("cascades") where multiple components need coordinated gating (model variant, routing, reranker config, and cache warmup).

Context and motivation:
- We keep seeing subtle emergent failures when an LLM-based reranker + new model + shard-level routing change are rolled independently. Failure modes show up only at intermediate traffic mixes.
- Goal: provide a reproducible playbook for experiments that must activate across several subsystems in lockstep, with clear SLO gates, observability checkpoints, and automated rollback hooks.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Orchestration pattern: staged cascade activation across components (model -> reranker -> routing -> cache priming).
- Measurement: which signals to watch and how to combine them into a single "go/no-go" decision.
- Allocation schedule templates (percent/time windows) and sample gating thresholds.
- Communication ritual: cross-team cadence and escalation matrix.
- Open questions / TODOs for follow-up experiments.

Definitions (short):
- Cascade: a coordinated activation where multiple infra/product pieces change activation state together (e.g., route 15% to model v2 AND enable reranker X for that cohort).
- Microcohort: a small user slice defined by traffic, geography, or product signal used for early validation.
- Signal fabric: the set of telemetry (latency, error, semantic regression metrics, business KPIs) used for gate decisions.

Roles and responsibilities (suggested):
- Release Owner (RO): product PM (owns hypothesis and final go/no-go).
- Deployment Lead (DL): infra/serving engineer (runs the rollout actions, toggles routes).
- Observability Steward (OS): SRE/observability (owns dashboards and alert fine-tuning).
- Safety Steward (SS): trust/safety or applied ML (approves semantic quality gates).
- On-call rota: include DL + OS for the 48h post-activation window.

Pre-launch checklist (practical):
- Confirm model variant is pinned and artifact hash available (GH PR or S3 path).
- Smoke tests: run 'simulated' traffic harness for 1000 synthetic requests covering edge intents.
- Synthetic regressions: run evaluation suite on baseline prompt set (perf + quality).
- Observability probes: pre-created dashboards and ratio-based alerts for the cascade.
- Rollback playbook: tested script to flip routing back & pin previous model.
- Stakeholder comms: publish activation plan to #release-orchestra and update Confluence page.

Signal fabric (priority signals to watch):
1) Latency signals
   - p50/p90/p99 for end-to-end (app -> model -> reranker).
   - GPU host queue length and kernel OOM rates.
   - Threshold example: p99 increase > 30% vs baseline for 10m -> pause escalation.
2) Error and reliability
   - API 5xx rate, request timeouts, partial payload errors.
   - Threshold: 5xx rate > 0.5% absolute increase -> immediate rollback.
3) Semantic quality (business-facing)
   - Evaluation delta on prioritized prompt set: rouge/bleu-like proxies, reranker NDCG, or human-labeled pass rate.
   - Threshold: drop in pass-rate >= 3pp (percentage points) over a 1h window -> quarantine.
4) Safety signals
   - Toxicity score alerts, hallucination heuristics, policy triggers.
   - Any new policy-violation events observed in cohort -> immediate rollback + incident review.
5) Cost/throughput economics
   - Tokens per request, average GPU seconds per request.
   - Threshold: cost per active session > 2x expected for 30m -> hold.

Composite gating heuristic (operational):
- Use a weighted scoring heuristic: S_total = w_lat*L_norm + w_err*E_norm + w_q*Q_norm + w_safe*S_norm + w_cost*C_norm.
- Baseline weights suggestion (tunable): lat=0.3, err=0.25, qual=0.25, safe=0.15, cost=0.05.
- Escalation rule: if S_total crosses a configured threshold for a rolling 15m, stop the next allocation step and trigger human review.
- Note: normalize each signal to 0-1 by clipping at pre-defined worst-case; keep conservatively small gates early.

Sample allocation schedule (template A: cautious cascade, 48h runway):
- Step 0 (pre-warm): 0% traffic; run smoke & synthetic tests (T=-12h).
- Step 1 (validation microcohort): 0.5% traffic for 1h -> monitor signals.
   - Must meet p99 latency < baseline *1.15; 5xx delta < 0.2pp; semantic pass-rate drop < 1pp.
- Step 2 (small canary): 2% traffic for 3h -> monitor, human check at 1h & 3h.
- Step 3 (expanded canary): 8% traffic for 12h -> automated checks + manual sign-off.
- Step 4 (broad exposure): 25% traffic for 24h -> automated checks; if stable, move to 100% over 6-12h.
- Step X (rollback window): full rollback capability available at every step.

Fast-fail (accelerated) schedule (template B: low-risk change, 8h runway):
- 1% -> 5% after 30m -> 20% after 2h -> 100% after 4-6h, but with strict error latency gates and lower semantic tolerance.

Rollback decision matrix (practical):
- Immediate rollback triggers (automated): 5xx delta > 1pp, p99 > baseline*2, safety policy violation event, system OOM on serving hosts.
- Escalate-to-human triggers: composite score S_total > threshold or semantic drop > 3pp.
- Partial rollback patterns: (a) route only (b) disable reranker (c) revert model to v1. Choose minimal rollback to restore stability.

Observability & dashboards (concrete):
- Per-cohort dashboards grouped by allocation percentage showing: latency, 5xx, token-cost, semantic pass-rate, safety-policy-events.
- Synthetic canary probe runs every 10m that exercise the same prompt set used for offline evals.
- Heatmap view for signal divergence across microcohorts (geo, client-version).
- Configure alerting: dual-signal alerts (requires both latency OR error AND semantic regression to reduce noisy pages).

Cross-team comms and run cadence:
- Pre-rollout: 48h pre-announce on #release-orchestra with launch window, owner, DL, SS.
- Activation time: live play-by-play pinned thread in Slack + short status updates at each step.
- Checkpoint ceremony: 1h post-step manual sign-off required for steps >= expanded canary.
- Post-mortem: mandatory if rollback occurred. If stable, short 48h summary and a 14d retrospective.

Automation hooks and small ops improvements to build:
- Single API to declare a cascade plan (JSON) that the deployment system can execute with step timers and gating hooks.
- Composite-signal engine: take inputs from metrics platform and publish S_total to Slack/console.
- Canary traffic generator for deterministic synthetic runs.

Open questions / experiments to run:
- How to automatically weight semantic quality vs latency for different product surfaces? (investigate PROD-4823).
- Work out safe defaults for microcohort definitions when user privacy prevents fine-grained slicing.
- Experiment: run 100 small cascades (0.5%-2%) with different weightings and track false-positive rollback rates.

Notes to self (brainstorm fragments):
- Maybe create a "canary recipe" library with pre-validated templates for common change-types: model-only, reranker-only, routing-only, and full-cascade.
- Consider a "canary debt" concept: how often we rely on manual sign-off tracks technical debt in automation.
- Need tighter coupling with cost tooling (Optimize) so runs surface token/GPU cost deltas inline.

Immediate next steps (owner: Priya):
- Draft a lightweight JSON schema for a cascade plan (due: 2026-03-01).
- Schedule a 60m cross-team sync with DL, OS, and SS to validate gating thresholds (target: next Tue).
- Create the Confluence home (linked above) and add this doc as the lab notes.

References and links:
- Confluence: Cascade-Experimentation-Home (linked_artifacts above).
- JIRA: PROD-4823 (tracking composite signal engine).
- Slack: #release-orchestra thread (search: "cascade test Jan2026").

End of notes.

-- Priya (please iterate; rough draft)
